negative_control_policy: choose the least declared horizon at or above both finite input indices; if none exists, report CONTROL_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_GRAMMAR

reduction_guard.reason: The bind is the declared identity-verdict consumer and identity_verdict_definitional is its in-boundary branch; reduction must keep the task-declared verdict-consumer shape. Every parameter change is rechecked for grammar membership and separation.

out_of_envelope_declaration.proof_method: within_grammar_witness of any witness binding these continuations against l1-v0/v1/v2 returns false with reason BIND_CONTINUATION: every input atom of this grammar lies within the old declared index bound (delay_index_max 2), every race partner within race_partner_index_max 2 and every deadline horizon within {0,1,2}, so the new continuation map is the only failing dimension

declared_bounds_note: Complete enumeration of the finite constructor product: atoms = 1 + 2*(delay_index_max+1) = 7; contexts = non-empty well-typed op sequences up to context_depth_max with a deadline only as the final op; denominator is finite and closed. Bounds are deliberately aligned with the existing L1 index horizons (delay_index_max 2, partner 2, horizons {0,1,2}) so that an out-of-envelope witness fails the old grammars on exactly one dimension (BIND_CONTINUATION). B-01 shape note: the pair members of every separating witness are delay-equivalent (the theory's own identity criterion judges them the same), and the separating context is the observation layer; the same pair is not separated under the definitional layer (a bare deadline at or above both arrival rounds), which is exactly the 'identity verdict depends on observation layer' premise.
